clue.text: Very big obstacle for Christian from the French couple

parts.note: des is French for 'from the' (plural)
a couple is a pair

explanation.surface: Something hinders a Christian, with a French connection and a pair involved.
explanation.walkthrough: In Bunyan's The Pilgrim's Progress, Christian is imprisoned by Giant Despair in Doubting Castle, hence 'very big obstacle'.
explanation.definitionFit: Giant Despair is the ogre who captures the pilgrim hero of Bunyan's allegory, a huge hindrance on his journey.

clue.text: Provincial lady surprisingly defied all

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests the letters of defied all turning up in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A woman from the country unexpectedly flouted everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: E. M. Delafield wrote The Diary of a Provincial Lady, so the author is defined by her famous creation.
explanation.definitionFit: The novelist is best known for The Diary of a Provincial Lady, narrated by that title character.

clue.text: Crack troops presently for infantry officer

parts.note: the SAS is the British Special Air Service, an elite regiment
presently means soon

explanation.surface: Elite soldiers will shortly be joined by a foot soldier's commander.
explanation.walkthrough: Siegfried Sassoon wrote Memoirs of an Infantry Officer, the definition alluding to that book and to his own war service.
explanation.definitionFit: The war poet served as a foot-soldier lieutenant and titled a memoir after that rank.

clue.text: French nobleman let slip philosopher

parts.note: aristo, short for aristocrat, is the word for a French noble of the Revolution era

indicators.note: let slip has the letters of let slipping out of order

explanation.surface: A French aristocrat carelessly blurted out something about a thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'let slip' reads as 'blurted out', but 'slip' is the anagram signal working on the short word before it; aristo is the usual term for a French Revolution noble.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek thinker, pupil of Plato, is among the most famous thinkers of antiquity.

clue.text: Rubbish hotel provided for important US novelist

parts.note: rot means nonsense or rubbish
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A poor hotel was booked for a major American writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Philip Roth was a leading American author of fiction, writer of Portnoy's Complaint.

clue.text: Brownish site of Taj reveals terracotta figurine

parts.note: tan is a light brown colour
the Taj Mahal stands in Agra, India

explanation.surface: A tourist at the Taj Mahal uncovers a small clay statue.
explanation.definitionFit: Tanagra figures are small Greek clay statuettes named after the Boeotian town where many were found.

clue.text: Albee piece offers both sex and reformed characters

indicators.note: reformed means formed again, so the letters of both sex and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A play by Albee deals with both sexes and people who have mended their ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reformed characters' sounds like rehabilitated people; 'reformed' rearranges BOTH SEX AND and 'characters' just tells you letters are involved.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Albee wrote a short one-act play with this title in 1959.

clue.text: Henry Miller's new (former American) work

parts.note: ex means former

explanation.surface: A fresh book by Henry Miller, once from America.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry Miller's Nexus is the last part of his Rosy Crucifixion trilogy, so the opening name flags which work is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: The title is a novel, a piece of literary output by Henry Miller.

clue.text: Gino confused about old Carlo, the dramatist

indicators.note: about means going around, so the jumble of Gino wraps the next word
confused means the letters of Gino are muddled

explanation.surface: An Italian called Gino is muddled about a veteran playwright named Carlo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' gives GONI, the anagram of the name, and 'about' wraps it round the next word; Goldoni was the Venetian comic playwright.
explanation.definitionFit: Carlo Goldoni was an eighteenth-century Venetian playwright famed for his comedies.

clue.text: A repetitive strain injury's raising voice's pitch

parts.note: RSI is the abbreviation for repetitive strain injury, plus the S of the possessive

explanation.surface: An injury from repeated strain makes one's voice rise higher.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive 's supplies a letter here, giving A RSI'S run together.
explanation.definitionFit: In older usage the term meant the elevation of the voice in pitch or stress, as opposed to thesis.

clue.text: Nicholas King's favourite writers included this novelist

indicators.note: included means the letters sit inside the words Nicholas King's

explanation.surface: A man named Nicholas King lists favourite writers, with this author among them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'favourite writers' is padding for the surface; the author Marghanita Laski is found spanning nichoLAS KIng.
explanation.definitionFit: Marghanita Laski was an English writer of fiction such as The Victorian Chaise-Longue.

clue.text: Some émigrés of Henry Treece

explanation.surface: Expatriates who appear in a book by Henry Treece.
explanation.definitionFit: Émigrés are people living away from their homeland, and Henry Treece wrote a historical novel of that title.

clue.text: Behaves like Wordsworth's cloud

parts.note: recalls the poem 'I wandered lonely as a cloud / That ... on high o'er vales and hills'

explanation.surface: Someone acts like the cloud in Wordsworth's daffodil poem.
explanation.definitionFit: Wordsworth's cloud drifts on high over the hills, so acting like it means drifting in the air.

clue.text: Mann is so imprecise about these houses

indicators.note: imprecise suggests Mann is so set down inexactly, with letters out of place

explanation.surface: Thomas Mann is vague when he writes about some homes.
explanation.definitionFit: Large stately homes are grand dwellings.

clue.text: Reading kept him indoors,

parts.note: Reading is the town whose gaol held a famous Irish writer, not the act of reading books

explanation.surface: A bookworm stays at home because of all his reading.
explanation.walkthrough: Capital R is disguised at the start; the author of The Ballad of Reading Gaol was imprisoned there in 1895–97.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish playwright was jailed in Reading Gaol for gross indecency.

clue.text: Surrealist in the modern style

indicators.note: in means the artist sits inside the words modern style

explanation.surface: A Surrealist painter working in a contemporary manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Max Ernst was a German painter of the Dada and Surrealist movements.

clue.text: "Cattle that have been — abroad, because they durstna bide at hame" (Rob Roy, Walter Scott)

definitions.text: "Cattle that have been — abroad, because they durstna bide at hame" (Rob Roy, Walter Scott)

parts.words: Cattle that have been — abroad, because they durstna bide at hame
parts.note: a line from Scott's Rob Roy with a Scots word for soldiering missing from the gap

explanation.surface: A Scots quotation from Rob Roy with one word blanked out.
explanation.walkthrough: Fill the gap from Scott's text; the missing word is Scots dialect for serving as soldiers (sodger = soldier).
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots a sodger is a soldier, so the word means serving in the army, as in the quoted line.

clue.text: Priedieus specially set up for playwright

indicators.note: specially set up means the letters of priedieus are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: Prayer desks have been specially arranged for a dramatist.
explanation.definitionFit: Euripides was one of the three great tragic dramatists of ancient Athens.

clue.text: Present for Mr Follett? (possibly from bookshop)

definitions.text: Present for Mr Follett? (possibly from bookshop)

parts.words: Present for Mr Follett? (possibly from bookshop)
parts.note: a present for the thriller writer Ken Follett, read as a phrase, describes a voucher one may buy from a bookshop

explanation.surface: A gift for the novelist Ken Follett, perhaps bought in a bookshop.
explanation.definitionFit: A voucher exchangeable for goods, such as a book voucher, makes a common present.

clue.text: One of those evidencing 1 Across in Barstow story

definitions.text: One of those evidencing 1 Across in Barstow story

parts.words: One of those evidencing 1 Across in Barstow story
parts.note: someone showing hopelessness, as in Stan Barstow's story collection The ...

explanation.surface: A character in a Stan Barstow tale who shows hopelessness.
explanation.walkthrough: The Spanish root means 'despairing', which is why such an outlaw shows 1 Across.
explanation.definitionFit: The word comes from Spanish for one in despair, a reckless outlaw with nothing to lose.

clue.text: At least 28 lines of verse

parts.note: fourteen-line poems, so two or more of them amount to at least 28 lines

explanation.surface: A minimum of twenty-eight lines of poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: Each such poem has fourteen lines, so a plural means two or more and so 28 lines at least.

clue.text: Licentious eighteenth-century writer starts really erotic tale in French

indicators.note: starts means the opening letters of the following five words

explanation.surface: A rakish eighteenth-century author begins a truly racy story in French.
explanation.walkthrough: Restif (or Rétif) de la Bretonne was a French writer of libertine novels.
explanation.definitionFit: Rétif de la Bretonne wrote scandalous and sexually frank works in eighteenth-century France.

clue.text: Heavy weight on certain footing, borne by Cadfael

indicators.note: on, in a down clue, puts the weight above the next piece

parts.note: a ton is a large unit of weight
sure means certain, and here it forms the footing at the base

explanation.surface: A heavy load rests on firm ground, carried by the medieval detective monk.
explanation.walkthrough: Cadfael is Ellis Peters' Benedictine monk-detective, who wears the monk's shaved crown.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaved patch on the crown is the haircut of a medieval monk such as Brother Cadfael.

clue.text: Enthusiast (a dramatist) gets the point in Hawthorne's work

parts.note: a fan is an enthusiast
George Bernard Shaw is the Irish playwright
E, east, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A fan of a playwright finds the key moment in a Hawthorne novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Hawthorne's first novel, published anonymously in 1828, bears this title.

clue.text: Foreign Office gets to fuel up in early edition

indicators.note: up, in a down clue, means the word for fuel is read bottom to top

parts.note: oil is a fuel

explanation.surface: The Foreign Office refuels in readiness for a first printing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' gives LIO, the fuel word backwards, as this is a down clue; the First Folio of Shakespeare is the classic case.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's First Folio is the classic example of an early large-format printing.

clue.text: "… those chambers held barbarian hordes / — foemen, and hot-blooded lords" (Keats)

definitions.text: "… those chambers held barbarian hordes / — foemen, and hot-blooded lords" (Keats)

parts.words: those chambers held barbarian hordes / — foemen, and hot-blooded lords
parts.note: lines from Keats's The Eve of St Agnes with the animal that describes the foemen missing

explanation.surface: A quotation from Keats with one word left blank.
explanation.walkthrough: The Eve of St Agnes describes the castle's 'barbarian hordes, / Hyena foemen, and hot-blooded lords'.
explanation.definitionFit: Keats likens the savage enemies to a scavenging African carnivore known for its laughing cry.

clue.text: Instrument gives back time

parts.note: the spine is the backbone, the back

explanation.surface: An instrument returns time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gives back' looks like a reversal signal; 'gives' is a link and 'back' supplies SPINE.
explanation.definitionFit: This small harpsichord is a keyboard instrument.

clue.text: Deceive exponent of two cultures

explanation.surface: Mislead the advocate of the two cultures idea.
explanation.definitionFit: To deceive with flattery is an American slang sense, and C. P. Snow expounded the arts-science divide in The Two Cultures.

clue.text: A comeback for Nell the boot is put in for Welsh novelist

indicators.note: is put in means the boot is placed inside the reversed name
comeback means Nell is read backwards

parts.note: a welly is a wellington boot

explanation.surface: Nell gets a kicking as a Welsh writer makes a return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comeback' gives LLEN, the name backwards, and 'is put in' places the British word for a rubber wellington boot inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Llewellyn wrote How Green Was My Valley, set among Welsh mining villages.

clue.text: Ellen Gilchrist offered it with affection

definitions.text: Ellen Gilchrist offered it with affection

parts.words: Ellen Gilchrist offered it with affection
parts.note: Gilchrist's story collection is titled with this word followed by 'With Love', and affection stands for love

explanation.surface: The writer Ellen Gilchrist gave something lovingly.
explanation.walkthrough: Ellen Gilchrist's 1986 collection is Drunk With Love; 'with affection' replaces 'with love'.
explanation.definitionFit: Intoxicated is the plain sense, and with love completes Gilchrist's book title.

clue.text: Agents ring changes where actors work

parts.note: a ring is round, the shape of the letter O

indicators.note: changes means the letters are altered in order

explanation.surface: Theatrical agents make phone calls to change things for performers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' looks like a phone call but is O, shuffled with AGENTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Performers play in front of the audience on the boards of the theatre.

clue.text: Film featuring blustering squire

explanation.surface: A movie with a loud country landowner in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowboy movie is one genre, and Squire Western is the bluff landowner in Fielding's Tom Jones.
